key_insight: SwimBird enables multimodal LLMs to dynamically switch between textual Chain-of-Thought and visual latent ‘thoughts’, improving vision-heavy reasoning without degrading text-based logical reasoning.
problem_solved: Existing MLLMs either rely mainly on textual CoT (weak for vision-intensive tasks) or inject fixed visual latents (which can harm text reasoning); SwimBird addresses the need for an adaptive, switchable reasoning mode in hybrid autoregressive MLLMs.
method: Hybrid autoregressive backbone that natively supports both token-based textual reasoning and continuous visual latent states.
A lightweight switchable reasoning mechanism (e.g., learned mode tokens/gating or attention control) that toggles when to use textual CoT versus injected visual thoughts during decoding.
Training and prompting strategy that mixes text-only and vision-text examples so the model preserves strong logical text reasoning while activating visual reasoning only when needed.
impact: Allows practitioners to deploy a single MLLM that adapts its internal reasoning style to task demands, improving performance on vision-intensive tasks without sacrificing language-based logic — simplifying model design and reducing the need for task-specific fine-tuning.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing hybrid autoregressive flow with a mode switch (textual CoT path vs. visual latent path).
Decision flow illustrating when the model toggles modes (example image + question → visual mode; pure text prompt → textual mode).
Bar chart comparing vision-task vs. text-reasoning performance for baseline, fixed-visual-latent, and SwimBird.
Token-level timeline visualization showing interleaving of textual tokens and injected visual latent vectors during decoding.
paper_title: SwimBird: Eliciting Switchable Reasoning Mode in Hybrid Autoregressive MLLMs
paper_authors: Jintao Tong, Shilin Yan, Hongwei Xue, Xiaojun Tang, Kunyu Shi
